metadata.source: Nick Hegyesi Oakridge old-growth deep research
metadata.accuracy_policy: Representative/estimated coordinates are research and navigation seeds, not exact tree coordinates. Coordinate caveats remain explicit per feature.
metadata.cultural_site_policy: Jim's Creek intentionally uses a broad landscape pin; do not infer or publish individual culturally modified tree coordinates.
metadata.temporary_status_policy: Closure/access statements are dated observations as of 2026-10-05 and must not be interpreted as permanent status.

properties.name: Greenwaters Trail Old Growth
properties.summary: Accessible old-growth Douglas-fir forest along the Middle Fork Willamette on the edge of Oakridge. The pin represents the trail/park old-growth area rather than an individual tree.
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Salmon Creek Falls Old-Growth Forest
properties.coordinate_type: official USFS facility/location point representing surrounding old-growth forest
properties.access: Public Salmon Creek area. Developed campground/day-use facilities were closed for the 2026 season; verify current USFS conditions before visiting.
properties.summary: Lush old-growth forest along Salmon Creek with pools and small falls. This is the same location as the prior approximate research pin near 43.76206, -122.37522; the official USFS point is used here.
properties.source: US Forest Service — Salmon Creek Falls Campground and Day Use
properties.temporary_access_status: Developed campground/day-use site closed for 2026 season; reopening anticipated spring 2027.
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Larison Rock Lower Old Growth
properties.coordinate_type: representative lower-trail old-growth pin; not an exact tree/grove coordinate
properties.access: Larison Rock Trail #3607. Hiking, horses and mountain biking are supported uses; research noted seasonal MTB restrictions Nov–Mar.
properties.summary: Lower Larison Rock Trail passes through substantial old-growth Douglas-fir and western hemlock forest. The pin represents the lower old-growth portion of the trail, not the summit or a single tree.
properties.source: US Forest Service — Larison Rock Trail #3607
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Larison Creek Old-Growth Corridor
properties.species: Douglas-fir; western hemlock; western redcedar; incense cedar
properties.coordinate_confidence: Very High for lower access; corridor extends beyond pin
properties.coordinate_type: lower trailhead/access point for a linear old-growth corridor
properties.access: Lower trailhead shown. Significant mature forest continues roughly 6.3 miles toward the upper trailhead at approximately 43.6845, -122.5291.
properties.summary: A 6.3-mile old-growth corridor containing Douglas-fir, western hemlock, western redcedar and incense cedar. This point marks lower access; it does not represent one isolated grove.
properties.source: US Forest Service — Larison Creek Trail #3646
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Jim's Creek Heritage Pine–Oak Landscape
properties.coordinate_type: broad project-area center; intentionally not an individual culturally modified tree
properties.access: Broad project-area location only. Do not use this pin to seek individual culturally modified trees.
properties.summary: Restored Oregon white oak–ponderosa pine cultural landscape with large heritage ponderosa pines. Some trees show evidence of traditional Indigenous bark harvesting; the pin intentionally represents the broader landscape, not individual culturally modified trees.
properties.source: US Forest Service — Jim's Creek project
properties.sensitive_location_policy: Do not publish, infer, or geocode individual culturally modified / medicine-tree locations.
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Tall Trees Grove / Trail #4269
properties.coordinate_type: estimated grove/trail area from USFS access directions
properties.access: Use official USFS access information. Research road sequence: FR18 → FR1817 → FR1806 → FR427.
properties.summary: Exceptional roughly 50-acre tall-tree forest with Douglas-firs about 270–310 feet tall, including specimens exceeding 300 feet. Pin is representative; navigate using official USFS access information.
properties.notable_dimensions: Douglas-fir approximately 270–310 ft tall; specimens exceeding 300 ft
properties.source: US Forest Service — Tall Trees Trail #4269
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Constitution Grove
properties.coordinate_type: estimated grove/access area from USFS directions
properties.access: Short interpretive loop; forest-road travel is considerably longer than straight-line distance suggests.
properties.summary: Classic old-growth Douglas-fir grove on an elevated river bench with western hemlock and western redcedar. USFS notes that many trees were already alive when the U.S. Constitution was signed.
properties.source: US Forest Service — Constitution Grove Trail #3675
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: Joe Goddards Grove
properties.species: Douglas-fir; western redcedar; western hemlock; Pacific yew
properties.coordinate_type: estimated grove area from USFS legal description and road information
properties.access: Primary trailhead was closed for post–Cedar Creek Fire impacts and hazards as of 2026-10-05. Verify current USFS conditions before travel.
properties.summary: Exceptional ancient grove containing Douglas-fir, western redcedar, western hemlock and giant Pacific yews. USFS documents trees roughly 450–700 years old and up to 116+ inches in diameter. Representative pin only.
properties.notable_dimensions: Old-growth trees about 40–116+ in diameter; historically measured tree about 251 ft tall
properties.source: US Forest Service — Joe Goddards Grove Trail #3690
properties.temporary_access_status: Primary access closed for Cedar Creek Fire impacts/hazards as of research date; verify current conditions.
properties.land_manager: US Forest Service / Willamette National Forest

properties.name: South Waldo Mountain-Hemlock Old Growth
properties.access: Access may be affected by Cedar Creek Fire closures depending on approach. Verify current conditions; no permanent open/closed state is asserted.
properties.summary: High-elevation mountain-hemlock old growth south of Waldo Lake, with old spruce and mature subalpine forest. A distinct ecosystem from Oakridge's lower-elevation Douglas-fir and cedar forests.

properties.name: Shale Ridge Cedar Grove
properties.access: Remote bottomland grove; verify current access conditions before visiting.
properties.summary: Remote bottomland grove of enormous western redcedars along braided North Fork Middle Fork Willamette channels. Some cedars are reported around eight feet in diameter.
properties.notable_dimensions: Western redcedars reported around 8 ft diameter
properties.source: Trailkeepers of Oregon / Oregon Hikers — Shale Ridge Cedar Grove
properties.source_quality: community-primary-for-location; no dedicated current USFS inventory page identified in research
